newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says to keep stronger crown fixing.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says to keep stronger crown fixing.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Wednesday said it was ready to continue, as long as necessary, fixing the crown stronger than the market rate to keep it stable and support it against speculative downward pressure.

"Regarding the stability of the currency we are ready to fix it at around current levels (of the NBS fixing) for some time longer, as long it will be necessary," NBS Treasury Director Frantisek Szulenyi told Reuters.

The NBS on Wednesday, for the third consecutive day, fixed the crown at 78 basis points below the mark/dollar basket parity while at the time of the fixing calculation, the crown was trading lower on the interbank market at -1.09 percent versus parity.
"We would not like to see the crown going down on short-term speculations and that is why we will fix it some time longer in a narrow corridor at around current fixing," Szulenyi said.

"Our monetary programme for 1997 says that we will be using the crown's fluctuation band more effectively and significantly than last year, but the current situation is specific and it thus requires a specific approach," Szulenyi said.

He would not say how long the NBS intended to maintain the current fixing levels. The central bank fixes the crown daily at around 0940 GMT within a band of plus/minus 7.0 percent around the midpoint.
Szulenyi said the NBS has not so far seen stronger longer-term downward pressure on the Slovak currency.
The Slovak crown weakened sharply on Wednesday morning in a round of speculative selling started by local banks. But foreign purchases of cheap crowns helped the currency firm slightly soon after.

The crown touched levels of 170 basis points on the depreciation side shortly after Wednesday's open, but it then firmed to around -1.30 percent against midpoint and hovered slightly below -1.00 percent until the NBS fixing.
Local traders said stronger NBS fixing helped the crown strengthen at around 100 basis points below the parity and gave it potential to strengthen further.
Some dealers said the crown could even move to around 25 basis points on the depreciation side of parity. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
